cells.tense: What you set in order is finished now, and nothing on it is still owed.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Pick something you finished and set right. Sit with it two minutes, just as it is, no fixing. Enjoying it is the whole visit; then leave it where it does.
cells.core:
You are at the part where things get finished. What you committed to has been tested by use, the tiring stretches are sorted, and you can stand in the result with your work done.

Growth here doesn't want pushing. Care that doesn't drain you, holding without gripping — that has been the method. So take the pleasure that's already sitting there: pick something you finished and set right, sit with it two minutes, just as it is, no fixing. Enjoying it is the whole visit; then leave it where it does. That rest is the last step of the making, not a payment. Two minutes, done, is enough.
cells.sheetLine: What careful work made is ready to enjoy.
cells.verb: Pressure-testing a commitment behind closed doors
cells.place: Where work is finished and carried across

cells.tense: Something is almost finished, and you are already bracing for what runs at you next.
cells.act: give directions plainly, once, and let them walk
cells.ask: Think of one person starting a thing you just finished. Say the one turn that mattered, once, then stop. Don't follow up; their walking it is the finish.
cells.core:
The finishing is barely done and the bracing has already started. A thing gets carried across and you are rehearsing the passage after it, ahead of everything still here and open. What's being tested is whether the commitment holds once the work is whole.

Direction pointed outward is the way back. Think of one person starting a thing you just finished. Say the one turn that mattered, once, then stop. Don't follow up; their walking it is the finish. Handing someone the route puts you at the start of something again, which is roughly where you are — and the bracing goes quiet.

cells.tense: Something you had a hand in was already carried across, and you have not let your hands off it.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Pick someone carrying something today. Take one real piece of weight off them — an errand, a shift, a call — and carry it to done. Then let the load be lighter and stop there.
cells.core:
A finished thing can leave your hands cleanly. The work is whole, the making is done, and it moves into what comes next without you standing over it. Here the letting-off has gone slow, and an hour that something ready to move is still being held.

Strength turns outward first. Pick someone carrying something today. Take one real piece of weight off them — an errand, a shift, a call — and carry it to done. Then let the load be lighter and stop there. You get to watch a thing end whole and set down, which is the move your own hands are still waiting to make.

cells.tense: You did the patient work that made this come out well, and you say it just happened.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Lie down or sit still a few minutes with no task and no fixing — just where the good result is now. Rest there, and let the rest count as the doing.
cells.core:
Someone has been holding things so they could grow — turns taken, pieces kept light, the small adjustments that let a result arrive. Asked about any of it, the answer is that it sort of made itself. The work is real; no name sits on it.

Growth comes back as itself, smaller and earlier: the patient part, before the abundance. Lie down or sit still a few minutes with no task and no fixing — just where the good result is now. Rest there, and let the rest count as the doing. Naming your part doesn't load it with anything. It puts the pen where it was already held.
